chunks: From him, from Salamah, from Yahya, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his grandfather, from Habba al-Urani, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever entrusts a man with his blood (life/lieutenant of his sword) and that man betrays him, then I am free from the killer, even if the slain is in the Hellfire.'

key_terms.دَمِهِ: His blood/life (metaphor for entrusting one's life)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on betrayal when one person entrusts another with their life in battle?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *amanah* (trust) in the context of blood-guarantee or military command, declaring that betrayal by the entrusted party absolves the guarantor of liability, even if the victim is destined for Hell. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the intrinsic spiritual status of the deceased and the legal consequences of the betrayer's action, emphasizing that the act of treachery itself constitutes a form of killing. The narration underscores the gravity of breaking trust in life-and-death matters, a key theme in Imam Ali’s governance and judicial rulings.
